text.p: Transport, logistics and security group Brambles Industries Ltd said on Friday it expected profit growth in the year ended June 30, 1997 but added that the growth would be hard won.

"We have budgetted for profit growth this year but it will be hard won and will not be helped by any significant recovery across our markets until the final quarter of the year at best," said Brambles chairman Alan Coates told the annual meeting.
Brambles posted a net profit of A$215.1 million for the year to June 30, 1996.
Coates said that conditions in the group's Australian operations remained extremely difficult, with little evidence of real strength in those sectors of the economy serviced by the company.
"While there is evidence that activity in the sectors has bottomed, particularly in housing, recovery will be slow," he said.

Brambles' wholly owned European operations were seen making higher profits in 1996/97 with improving prospects in future years for all divisions including the CHEP pallet pool, Coates said. "We have the greatest confidence in the continued rapid growth of our pooling system in the (European) region," he said.
Coates said Brambles was anxious to growt the mainland European business and it had a number of discussions in hand which could lead to substantial expansion.

In Brambles' U.S. waste operations, its incineration facility was profitable and its outlook had improved, while its landfill operations were facing a tighter access to waste, Coates said. He noted CHEP pallet operations were trialling a plastic pallet which might replace conventional wood pallets.
